findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In `review_plan_start`, resolve the engine inside the `anyio.to_thread.run_sync` worker, before `_start_gate_job` and the variant are built. `ConfigError` still fails the start before any job is created.
evidence: Plan: "Each tool resolves the engine ONCE (`resolve_plan_review_engine(engine)` against the server's config)"
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:315 — `return _config.compose_config(repo_root).verify.plan_review_engine` on the None path

src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:288-293 — "Basis resolution and index writes block, so keep them off the event loop." / "The material read for the dedup variant is a store read too, so it runs in the worker thread with the rest of the start."
findings.finding: For the async `review_plan_start` tool, the plan says to resolve the engine once (`resolve_plan_review_engine(engine)` against the server's config) before any job is created. It does not say this must run inside the existing `anyio.to_thread.run_sync` worker. When `engine` is None, `resolve_plan_review_engine` calls `compose_config(repo_root)`, which is a blocking config read. The current tool deliberately keeps every blocking read (basis resolution, the material read for the variant, index writes) off the event loop. An implementer who resolves at the top of the async function, before the `await`, would block the event loop.
findings.location: Approach → MCP bullet ('Each tool resolves the engine ONCE ...'); src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py review_plan_start
scenarios: An MCP client issues `review_plan_start` with no engine while other tools are being served; the config read runs on the event loop and stalls concurrent requests.
findings.suggested_fix: Inside the worker lambda/closure: `resolved = resolve_plan_review_engine(engine)` first, then `_start_gate_job(..., variant=_plan_review_variant(ticket_id, source, resolved), work=lambda: _review_plan_body(ticket_id, ref, source, force, readonly=ro, engine=resolved))`. A `ConfigError` raised there propagates out of `run_sync` before `begin_gate_job` is called, so the 'no job created' test still holds.
